data.name: mLST8
data.description: mLST8 (GbetaL) - a shared subunit of BOTH mTOR complexes. Especially required for mTORC2 to assemble and signal to Akt; largely dispensable for mTORC1.
data.description_beginner: A small building block shared by both mTOR complexes, but it matters much more for mTORC2 - without it, mTORC2 can't properly assemble and signal to Akt, while mTORC1 mostly works fine without it.

reading_levels.beginner: A shared subunit that matters more to mTORC2.
reading_levels.student: GβL; present in both complexes but essential only for mTORC2 in vivo.
reading_levels.research: Knockout phenocopies Rictor rather than Raptor loss, which is the standard genetic argument that mLST8 is an mTORC2-essential component.

studies.title: GbetaL, a positive regulator of the rapamycin-sensitive pathway required for the nutrient-sensitive interaction between raptor and mTOR
studies.authors: Kim DH; Sarbassov DD; Ali SM; Latek RR; Guntur KVP; Erdjument-Bromage H; Tempst P; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Discovered mLST8 (GbetaL), the third core subunit that clamps onto mTOR's kinase domain and stabilizes the complex. It fine-tunes how tightly Raptor holds mTOR in response to nutrients - a small but essential cog that later turned out to be especially critical for the mTORC2 complex.

studies.title: Ablation in mice of the mTORC components raptor, rictor, or mLST8 reveals that mTORC2 is required for signaling to Akt-FOXO and PKCalpha, but not S6K1
studies.authors: Guertin DA; Stevens DM; Thoreen CC; Burds AA; Kalaany NY; Moffat J; Brown M; Fitzgerald KJ; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The foundational genetic 'dissection' of the two complexes in living mice. Deleting Raptor was lethal early (mTORC1 essential); deleting Rictor or mLST8 selectively knocked out mTORC2 signaling to Akt and PKCalpha but spared S6K1. This cleanly assigned jobs to each complex and showed mLST8 is an mTORC2-specific requirement in mice.

studies.title: Structure of the human mTOR complex I and its implications for rapamycin inhibition
studies.authors: Yip CK; Murata K; Walz T; Sabatini DM; Kang SA

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human mTORC1 purified from HEK-293T cells stably expressing FLAG-raptor; negative-stain and cryo-EM (26 A); antibody labelling; in vitro kinase assays on S6K1 and 4E-BP1 with FKBP12-rapamycin or Torin1
studies.finding: The authors purified intact, active human mTORC1 and solved its shape by cryo-electron microscopy at about 26 angstrom resolution. The complex is an obligate dimer with a rhomboid outline and a central cavity, held together by interlocking contacts between mTOR and Raptor; antibody labelling placed mLST8 at the outer 'feet' and PRAS40 next to Raptor. Exposing purified mTORC1 to FKBP12-rapamycin first added a bound density in about 10% of particles, then broke the complex apart, with virtually no intact particles left after one hour, while the ATP-competitive inhibitor Torin1 left it intact. In matching kinase assays, FKBP12-rapamycin blocked S6K1 phosphorylation quickly but 4E-BP1 phosphorylation only after at least 60 minutes, and Raptor-free mTOR still phosphorylated S6K1 (rapamycin-sensitively) but not 4E-BP1. The authors proposed that rapamycin inhibits the two substrates by different mechanisms. Boundary: Purified protein and low-resolution EM; the authors note that in cells rapamycin neither fully blocks 4E-BP1 phosphorylation nor dismantles mTORC1, so the disassembly model is an in vitro result.

relations.mechanism: mLST8 is dispensable for mTORC1 in vivo but essential for mTORC2 - a rare clean genetic separation of the two complexes.
relations.mechanism_beginner: This protein isn't needed for mTORC1 in a living animal, but mTORC2 can't work without it – a clean genetic way to tell the two complexes apart.
relations.boundary: Knockout mice (GUE2006) and human cell biochemistry (KIM2003). The separation of the two complexes is shown in mouse tissue; whether it holds in human tissue is not tested by these studies.
relations.note: The cleanest genetic argument that the two complexes are truly separate machines.
